crm_notes:
- Mid-market SaaS vendor (ITSM product) building an internal IT/helpdesk assistant for agents and internal ops.
- Primary focus: sub-200ms p90 for short turn, streaming responses desirable.
- Wants tool-calling surface to run ticket updates (Jira/Snow) from chat.
- Start on Hosted API, evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity if latency/cost tradeoffs require it.
- Security: SSO (SAML), audit logs with retention controls (wants 12mo by default), KMS for key management.
- "Quote: 'We need answers fast — 200ms or we lose context in the agent workflow.'"
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit for predictable latency but needs pricing tiers for bursts.
- POC focus: 1) latency profile for short query+tool-call (ticket fetch/update), 2) streaming & partial completion, 3) audit log shape and retention export.
- Also asked about model fallback: prefer Redwood-managed fallbacks (smaller quantized model) vs. outright throttling.
- Legal asked for SOC2/ISO artifacts; security requested design for retention purging and export APIs.
- AE note: strong champion in Head of Product (Lina Torres).
requirements_summary: Latency SLO: p90 < 200ms for text-only short queries; streaming start-of-response < 100ms desirable. Throughput: 200 concurrent agents during peak. Tool-calling: secure connector to Jira/ServiceNow with audit trails. Data residency: US. Retention: configurable, default 12 months, ability to export logs. Authentication: SSO (SAML) + RBAC for admin console. Observability: per-route latency/cost breakdown, token-level trace for samples.
poc_scope: 2-week POC: Hosted API small-scale - 50 agents, simulate 200 concurrent short queries to measure p50/p90/p99 latency.
Streaming test: measure time-to-first-byte and partial deltas for streaming responses under load.
Tool-calling test: demo secure Jira update flow, show audit log entries for each call (immutable, exportable).
Failover test: force hosted capacity cutover to smaller quantized model and measure UX regression.
Ops/Cost: run cost model comparison (hosted vs. dedicated reserved) for projected 6/12 month volumes.
